shots.text: Water. In every direction... only water.
No coastline. No ship. No sound —
except the slap of waves against a piece of wood barely wider than a door.
And on that piece of wood... a young man is waking up.
His name is Teo. He doesn't remember falling asleep. He doesn't remember the storm.
All he knows is this: the horizon is perfectly flat... and it's empty.
He moves too fast. The wood tilts — and the ocean nearly takes him.
Then he hears it. A cough.
Twenty meters away, a hand rises out of the water... gripping the edge of a floating door.
shots.subject: other
other
shots.text: Her name is Mara.
It takes Teo four tries to reach her... the board spinning like a leaf.
When he finally pulls her aboard, the two of them barely fit. Two strangers. One plank.
And no idea how long they'll be out here. Every wave that washes over the edge reminds them:
this board was never meant to carry two people. Mara looks at the door she was clinging to...
"Get it," she says. "We tie them together." It's the first thing they ever build.
Two pieces of wood. One knot. One slightly bigger island.
Around them, the ocean is littered with the remains of the storm.
Mara is the first to start counting. A plastic tarp. A coil of rope. A small folding knife. Three empty bottles.
It doesn't look like much. But survivors have a saying — a rough rule of thumb:
Three hours without shelter... three days without water... three weeks without food.
They have shelter... barely. Food can wait. Water is the clock that's already ticking.
By afternoon, the sun is merciless. Teo's lips crack.
He stares at the water all around him. Endless, cool, right there.
He cups his hands. Mara grabs his wrist. "Don't."

shots.subject: other
shots.text: The first night is the longest of their lives. They take turns sleeping — one always holding on.

shots.subject: other
shots.text: Mara barely speaks. Teo talks too much. About home. About food...

shots.subject: other
shots.text: He tells her he was on the ship as a cook's assistant... never been this far from land...

shots.subject: other
shots.text: ...he can't swim very well — which, he admits, is a funny thing to say out loud right now.

shots.subject: other
shots.text: Mara finally answers, eyes still closed. "Then don't let go."

shots.subject: other
shots.text: It's not comforting. But somehow, it helps.

shots.subject: other
shots.text: Above them, the sky is filled with more stars than Teo knew existed.

shots.subject: other
shots.text: No city lights. No pollution. Just the whole galaxy, spilled across the dark. Beautiful. And completely indifferent.

shots.subject: other
shots.text: And then, just before dawn... the air changes. It smells like rain.

shots.subject: other
shots.text: Mara moves faster than Teo has ever seen anyone move. She spreads the tarp...

shots.subject: other
shots.text: ...ties two corners to the board, pushes the center down into a bowl. "Hold this edge. Don't let it flip."

shots.subject: other
shots.text: The first drops hit the plastic like pebbles. Then the sky opens.

shots.subject: other
shots.text: Real survivors did exactly this.

shots.subject: other
shots.text: In 1942... Poon Lim... 133 days alone on a raft.

shots.subject: other
shots.text: (the tarp keeps filling)

shots.subject: other
shots.text: Mara and Teo don't know that yet. They just know the tarp is filling.

shots.subject: other
shots.text: They fill all three bottles. Teo drinks first. Then Mara. Slowly — she makes him slow down.

shots.subject: other
shots.text: For the first time since they woke up... Teo laughs. It's the best water either of them has ever tasted.

shots.subject: other
shots.text: But when Mara holds the bottles up to the light, the laughter stops.

shots.subject: other
shots.text: Three bottles. Two people. And the sky is already clearing. At this rate, it won't last three days.
Day two begins with a decision.

shots.subject: other
shots.text: Mara stands up — carefully — and turns slowly, scanning the water.

shots.subject: other
shots.text: The storm didn't just sink their ship. It scattered pieces of it across miles of ocean.

shots.subject: other
shots.text: A wooden pallet. A plastic crate. A long beam, floating just out of reach.

shots.subject: other
shots.text: "Everything that floats," she says, "is ours."

shots.subject: other
shots.text: Teo grins. For the first time, this feels less like waiting to die... and more like a plan.
They work with what they have.

shots.subject: other
shots.text: Teo paddles out using a broken plank as an oar, while Mara holds the rope tied around his waist...

shots.subject: other
shots.text: ...a lifeline, in case a wave takes him. The pallet comes first. Then the crate.

shots.subject: other
shots.text: Then, after almost an hour of fighting the current, the beam.

shots.subject: other
shots.text: Every piece gets lashed on with the knots Mara learned from her father: one to hold, one to lock, one more just in case.

shots.subject: other
shots.text: By evening, the two pieces of wood they woke up on have become seven.
It's still small. Still fragile. But now they can both lie down — at the same time. (both lying)
shots.subject: other
other
shots.text: Teo stretches out on the pallet like it's a hotel bed. "Floating kingdom," he announces. "Population: two."

shots.subject: other
shots.text: Mara rolls her eyes. But she doesn't correct him.
Third day, water runs out. They ration the last bottle.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: Mara stretches the tarp overhead.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: ...so the sun won't steal what little water is left.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: And then Teo notices something strange.
Fish. Small silver ones, gathered in the shadow beneath the raft.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: More than yesterday. Many more.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: Fish gather under floating objects.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: Fishing fleets drop floating rafts on purpose.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: Scientists still debate why. Shelter, food, maybe company.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: For two hungry people, the reason doesn't matter.
They have no hook. So they make one.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: Teo bends a staple with the knife handle until it curves.
Survivors have done this before.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: Some say from wire, others from a nail.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: For bait: a strip of cloth from Teo's shirt.
The first hour? Nothing.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: The second hour? A nibble. The hook slips free.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: Teo slams his fist on the wood.
Mara ties the line back on and hands it to him. Again.
shots.subject: other
other
shots.text: The third hour? The line goes tight.

shots.subject: other
shots.text: (fish on the hook)
A fish no longer than Teo's hand. A feast.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: Fresh fish holds water.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: That night, Teo can't stop smiling.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: Water from the sky! Food from below! We can do this!
Mara looks at the horizon: a wall of black cloud.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: Tie everything down, she says quietly.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: It hits just after midnight. The wind arrives first.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: It rips the tarp straight out of Teo's hands.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: Then, the waves. Not the gentle swells of the last two days.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: Moving hills of water, black and white capped.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: Lifting the raft high and dropping it into the trough.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: Mara ties a rope around her waist, then around Teo's, then to the beam.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: Whatever happens, don't let go of the raft, and don't let go of me.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: A wave breaks over them.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: No raft, no sky, only water.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: When they surface, gasping, Teo hears a sound worse than thunder.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: The crack of wood. The lashings on the far side have snapped.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: The pallet, the crate, the beam, all of it twisting away into the dark.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: Teo lunges after it. Mara pulls him back. Let it go!
shots.subject: other

shots.text: He wants to scream at her. Instead, he holds on.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: The storm lasts until dawn. When the sky turns grey, they're still there.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: Soaked, shivering, bruised, tied to each other.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: Three pieces of wood.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: No tarp, no bottles.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: The sea took almost everything back. Teo stares at what remains.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: Two days of work.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: Mara sits up slowly and starts to untie the rope from his waist.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: We're alive. The wood was just wood.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: By midday, the ocean is flat again, almost peaceful.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: Teo is lying on the board, staring at the sky.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: A bump. Something solid touched the raft from below.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: He sits up. Mara is already staring into the water.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: Nothing. Then, a shadow passes beneath them.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: Long, slow, much longer than the raft.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: The water lifts, as something enormous moves underneath.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: And then, it turns around. And comes back.
shots.subject: other

shots.text: Part two is already waiting.
